videos.title: How LEGO Bricks Are Made (A 1958 Brick Still Fits) 🧱
videos.description:
Plastic granules melted at 230 °C, blasted into steel molds accurate to thousandths of a millimeter, and out pops a brick in seconds. That precision is why a brick from 1958 still clicks into one made today, and only about 18 in a million get rejected.
What's the coolest thing you ever built? 👇

videos.title: How Is Chocolate Made? (It Starts Super Bitter) 🍫
videos.description:
From a fruit growing straight out of a tree trunk: bitter beans fermented under banana leaves for a week, roasted, ground into a liquid (half of it is fat), stirred for hours with sugar and milk, and tempered for the shine and the snap.
Dark, milk, or white: which team are you? 👇

videos.title: How Is Paper Made? (It Was 99% Water) 📄🌲
videos.description:
The recipe began in China around 105 AD. Today logs are chipped and cooked into soft fibers, sprayed as a 99% water pulp onto a mesh racing at 100 km/h, pressed, dried on steam cylinders, and recycled 5 to 7 times.
Paper books or screens: which do you read more? 👇
